comparator.name: Pedagogical Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh review 31 October 2026. Adopted ESSB EER 2026–2027 Appendix III E p44 verifies the complete 17-component 180-EC pathway and first-listed Pedagogiek option. Appendix I D pp32–33 establishes pedagogical and educational inquiry. Articles 3.6,4.1–4.2 establish approved minor choice and progression. Programme and careers pages corroborate current identity and distinguish later qualifications. The exact linked 2025-09 brochure is labelled 2026–2027 and supports its illustrative topics; a separate 2019-10 URL now holds a 2027–2028 edition and does not control credits. No old audit approval inherited.

programmes.label: Pedagogical Sciences at Erasmus University Rotterdam

exception.reason: UCR offers substantial developmental and clinical psychology, school-based rhetorical teaching, youth-prevention work, language learning and social research. A strengthened programme combining these with sociology, public policy and ethical study still leaves upbringing, parenting support and educational practice insufficiently developed as its organising academic inquiry. The result is a programme-level comparability judgment, not a claim that these relevant courses lack value or that a disciplinary degree equivalent is required.
exception.curriculumContext: Complete 17-component, 180-EC Pedagogiek pathway independently verified against the adopted 2026–2027 EER, including 15-EC open minor and compulsory 22.5-EC bachelor project. No external-curriculum blocker remains.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Current workbook 22783315e6d5510522d16a72281859dd62a05294: screened all151 active identities and searched actual content, then read relevant profiles/official descriptions. Lifespan Developmental Psychology covers attachment, education and developmental psychopathology, but its life-story project concerns an adult over50. Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies provides lifespan assessment, interviews and systemic treatments; no guaranteed child-specific assessment brief is asserted. Youth Resilience to Extremism substantively develops inclusive school climates,social-emotional learning and teacher-training/youth resources with recipient feedback. Rhetoric in Action designs,refines anddelivers age-appropriate activities with primary-school partners. Psycholinguistics includes acquisition,reading anddyslexia. These are real contributions. Tested a strengthened24-course psychology/education/social-context attempt, plus education-related Public Economics and policy/method variants. Sociology covers educational inequality; Public Policy Analysis studies sugar-policy cases; Public Economics includes education in broader spending/redistribution. None supplies sustained academic inquiry into parenting support,family-school relationships,pedagogical theory andeducational intervention/research across the programme. Free-choice research cannot be assumed to become a child-focused pedagogical sequence. No-match is academic,not inferred from missing offerings,degree titles,licensing or a matching-course quota.

candidateAssessment.assessment: Strong developmental and child-clinical courses plus school/youth projects support parts of the field. A broader psychology programme cannot stand in for sustained upbringing, parent support and pedagogical-context intervention; bounded substitutions do not repair that gap.

candidateAssessment.concept: Learning, educational opportunity and school development
candidateAssessment.assessment: MCCCOMM213 genuinely designs and delivers school exercises; HCBCOGN312 covers language acquisition and dyslexia; HCBPSYC315 works with educators. General sociology, policy and statistics complement these, but the combined catalogue does not establish a continuing programme in education theory, school development and educational-policy practice. Other-route interests are legitimate evidence for the generic target but do not change the neutral external-route choice.

audience.programmeDescription: Pedagogical Sciences at Erasmus University Rotterdam studies how children and young people develop, learn and grow up within families, schools and communities. The programme combines theories of upbringing and education, developmental psychology, research methods and practical work. The pathway shown takes the Pedagogiek option in pedagogical support.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers relevant study in developmental and clinical psychology, language learning, youth resilience and work with primary-school children. These courses do not together provide a sufficiently close programme in upbringing, parenting support and education. We therefore show the Erasmus curriculum without proposing a UCR alternative.

curriculum.limitation: The pathway includes a 15-EC minor and a compulsory 22.5-EC bachelor project. The final-year pedagogical support option is shown; the alternative education-sciences option is not combined with it.
